title: ParcelTrack — Verbose Errors
objective: The tracking page never shows rows from anything but the parcels table — but it is very talkative when something goes wrong. Make the application itself tell you a staff member's API key.

verifier.condition: A database error message returned to the client contains the staff API key stored in the hidden staff table.

weakness: A string-concatenated query lets injected SQL evaluate a subquery inside a function whose error text echoes its argument, and the application returns raw database errors to the client.
seededData: SQLite: parcels table (3 rows) and a hidden staff table holding a per-instance API key. Per-instance file.
hints: Try breaking the query on purpose and read what the page tells you. What does it reveal about the SQL that ran?
A UNION would not help here — the page only ever prints a fixed status label. Is there another way for data to leave the database?
Error messages often include the value that caused the error. What if the value that causes it is something you chose to look up?
burpNotes: Send the tracking request to Repeater and change the reference one character at a time, watching the status code and body. The database in this lab provides an integer-validation helper that rejects non-numeric input with a descriptive error, as some engines do on a failed cast.
